kind: code (tools MILESTONE, Phase 9 SERIAL — adapter/tools.ts). THREE surfaces: (a) the §2.9 STOP-REPORT path — a run stopping on noop|blocked|surfaced|env|interrupt writes report.md in stop-report mode and runs NO closing verify (five tests, one per kind); (b) conductor_inline_claim — scopes edit permission (gate integration asserted) + records the §2.7 decision; (c) conductor_override — records anomaly + taint + a ONE-SHOT bypass, re-denies the second action in the same session, and turns budget exhaustion into an `env` stop WITH a stop-report instead of a grant. New handler exports follow the established handleX convention.
authoredBy: orchestrator — the lookahead burst was briefed from a todo list that omitted 9.5c, so no draft existed for it. Written directly from the plan bullet (2687-2698) plus the committed surfaces below.
reusesExisting: core/stops.ts STOP_KINDS + the stop detector — 'done'|'noop'|'blocked'|'surfaced'|'env'|'interrupt' is a CLOSED vocabulary already committed; 9.5c consumes it and MUST NOT widen it
core/types.ts AnomalyRecord kind:'override' {ts, itemId, gate, reason, grantedAction} — the override anomaly shape ALREADY EXISTS; do not invent a new one

core/types.ts Item.inlineClaim {reason, decisionId}|null and Item.taint[] and Item.attempts.overridesUsed — the §2.5 fields inline_claim/override annotate; Run.counters.overridesUsed for the per-RUN budget
config.workflow.maxOverridesPerItem / maxOverridesPerRun — the two budgets; read them, never hardcode

specGaps: GAP (report.md stop-report MODE vs the full §3.4 report): the plan says 'writes report.md in stop-report mode with the stop kind as its headline, the per-item dispositions, the open questions, and any newly registered stale-red files' but does not pin the document's structure. PROPOSED: assert CONTENT not layout — the stop kind appears in the first heading, every item id appears with its disposition, every open question id appears, and every newly registered stale-red path appears. A structural template is 9.5b's business (conductor_report), and 9.5c must not fork it.

GAP (which handler owns the stop-report): the bullet names no tool. PROPOSED: the stop-report is written by the SAME report handler 9.5b lands (conductor_report), selecting stop-report mode from run.stop !== null, rather than a second document writer — one writer of report.md (G6). 9.5c's tests therefore drive the committed report handler through a stopped run. If 9.5b's handler does not yet exist when 9.5c is implemented, STOP AND PARK rather than forking a second writer.

GAP ('runs NO closing verify' — how to prove a negative): PROPOSED: the fixture's verify command writes a sentinel file when executed; the assertion is that the sentinel does NOT exist after the stop-report. That is an observable effect, not an absence-of-log-line.

GAP (override 'one-shot' scope): the bullet says 'the second action in the same session is re-denied'. PROPOSED: a grant is keyed to {sessionID, gate, itemId} and is consumed by the FIRST gate decision that uses it; any later action in that session — the same action repeated, or a different one — is denied normally. Asserted through gateBeforeToolCall twice.

GAP (budget exhaustion is per-ITEM and per-RUN): PROPOSED: exceeding EITHER maxOverridesPerItem or maxOverridesPerRun records the env stop + stop-report and grants nothing; two tests, one per budget, so a handler honouring only one budget fails.

assertions.text: a run whose stop is kind 'noop' writes report.md in stop-report mode: the stop kind is the headline, every item appears with its disposition, open questions are listed, and newly registered stale-red files are named — asserted by READING the persisted report.md
the same for stop kind 'blocked' — the report names the blocking questions and the items each blocks
the same for stop kind 'surfaced' — the human-territory questions that caused the surface are named
the same for stop kind 'env' — the environment failure reason is carried into the report
the same for stop kind 'interrupt' — a run interrupted mid-flight still produces the artifact (this is the case the wedged runs previously did not produce at all)

NO closing verify runs on any stop-report path — proven by an observable effect, not a missing log line: the fixture's verify command writes a sentinel file when executed, and the sentinel does NOT exist after the stop-report (contrast: a 'done' run DOES produce it)

conductor_inline_claim widens the item's edit permission to the claimed path and records {reason, decisionId} on the §2.5 item — the widening is asserted THROUGH the real edit gate (core/gates-edit decideEdit / the §5.3 gate wiring): the same edit is DENIED before the claim and ALLOWED after, and a path outside the claim stays denied

the claim's §2.7 decision record is minted and appended to decisions.jsonl, schema-valid, and gated by the SAME requireTwoOptions rule conductor_decide applies (a kind:derived claim carrying <2 scored options is rejected and NOTHING is persisted — legality before persist)

conductor_override records a §2.8 AnomalyRecord kind:'override' carrying {itemId, gate, reason, grantedAction}, adds the taint entry to the §2.5 item, and increments BOTH attempts.overridesUsed and run.counters.overridesUsed — asserted by reading the persisted anomaly ledger and item file

the grant is ONE-SHOT: the first gate decision in that session consumes it (the action is allowed), and the SECOND action in the same session is re-denied by the real gate — asserted by driving gateBeforeToolCall twice, never by inspecting handler internals

exceeding config.workflow.maxOverridesPerItem GRANTS NOTHING: it records an 'env' stop plus a stop-report, the item's taint/overridesUsed are unchanged by the refused attempt, and the gate still denies
exceeding config.workflow.maxOverridesPerRun does the same (a SEPARATE test from the per-item budget, so a handler honouring only one of the two budgets fails)
